answers.answer: Supported: The clean 2D bulk model is a strongly Rashba-coupled electron gas, H0=Σk f†k[εk−α(σxky−σykx)]fk with εk=k²/(2m)−μ, plus an in-plane Zeeman term. In the strong-SOC/weak-field limit, the two helical-band Eilenberger equations decouple: −ivF k̂·∇λgλ=[(iωn−Δ̂)τz,gλ], with ∇λ=∇−iQλ[τz,...], ωn=(2n+1)πT, and Δ̂=[[0,Δ(r)],[Δ*(r),0]]. The source also defines helical-band DOS and field-induced shifts in its bulk conventions.

answers.answer: Supported: The source distinguishes equilibrium/global and metastable/local branches. At increasing field, a local minimum of j(q) crosses zero, creates a free-energy minimum, and later becomes global, producing a jump in equilibrium q. Below TCEP, Ic− is determined by the local minimum nearest qs rather than the global minimum because continuous current reduction generally requires crossing a free-energy barrier. The source separately notes that domain motion, tunneling, and dissipative switching can change the experimentally realized current.
